news_summary: A remarkable cosmic event revealed that a black hole's destruction of a massive star may have left behind unexpected remnants, offering new insights into black hole and stellar interactions.
news_summary_fr: Un événement cosmique remarquable a révélé que la destruction d'une étoile massive par un trou noir aurait pu laisser derrière elle des vestiges inattendus, offrant ainsi un nouvel éclairage sur les interactions entre les trous noirs et les étoiles.
news_summary_es: Un extraordinario fenómeno cósmico ha revelado que la destrucción de una estrella masiva por parte de un agujero negro podría haber dejado tras de sí restos inesperados, lo que ofrece nuevos conocimientos sobre las interacciones entre los agujeros negros y las estrellas.

articles.title: A black hole shredded a “super sun” — but something strange may have survived
articles.summary: Astronomers have witnessed a black hole violently shredding a massive star, creating one of the most energetic stellar explosions ever observed. The event, nicknamed “the Whippet,” briefly released about 400 billion times the Sun’s energy and sent a shock wave racing outward at one-fifth the speed of light. Months later, scientists spotted unexpectedly fast-moving helium, suggesting that some structure may have survived the destruction.
articles.content:
A massive star has been torn apart and gradually consumed by a black hole in a spectacular event that scientists compared to "preparing a snack for lunch."

Astronomers around the world observed the extreme encounter, and the event was presented at the AAS conference in Phoenix, Arizona. Researchers described the star as being "torn up" as the immense gravity of the black hole pulled it apart and consumed its material piece by piece.

Associate Professor of Astrophysics Daniel Perley, of Liverpool John Moores University, is the lead author of a paper in the Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society. He told the conference: "We discovered what we think is a black hole merging with a massive companion star, shredding it into a disk that feeds the black hole. It's a rare and awe-inspiring phenomenon."

The destruction produced one of the most powerful cosmic events ever recorded. For a brief period, the energy being released reached roughly 400 billion times the output of Earth's Sun, surpassing even the most powerful supernovae known to astronomers.

Black Hole Devours a Massive Star

Astronomers have previously observed black holes apparently consuming stars in events known as Tidal Disruption Events. However, researchers had never seen one take place on a scale like this.

Anna Ho, an assistant professor of astronomy at Cornell University and a coauthor with Perley on the paper, identified the remarkable event soon after its light arrived at Earth. Using the Zwicky Transient Facility at Palomar Observatory in California, she detected the object, formally designated AT2024wpp and nicknamed the Whippet.

Researchers quickly suspected that the phenomenon could be a Luminous Fast Blue Optical Transient (LFBOT), a rare and poorly understood type of visible cosmic event linked to the destruction of stars. Within a day, observations from the Liverpool Telescope in the Canary Islands and NASA's Swift satellite in space showed that the object displayed the expected characteristics of an LFBOT. It appeared extremely blue and was producing X-rays.

Distance measurements supplied by coauthors R. Michael Rich at UCLA and Yu Jing Qin at Caltech showed that the transient was releasing far more energy than an ordinary supernova. Combined with other observations, including its exceptionally high temperature, the measurements led the researchers to conclude that they were witnessing a star being ripped apart and swallowed by a black hole.

"Even though we suspected what it was, it was still extraordinary," added Perley. "This was many times more energetic than any similar event and more than any known explosion powered by the collapse of a star.

"Not only do these events help us identify black holes, they provide a new way to identify where black holes occur and how they form and grow, and the physics of how this happens," Perley added.

Shock Wave Races Through Surrounding Gas

Additional studies of AT2024wpp indicate that the event generated a powerful shock wave that traveled outward through dense surrounding gas at one-fifth the speed of light. After about half a year, however, the shock suddenly appeared to "fizzle out."

Material pulled from the star formed a disk around the black hole and became intensely hot as it spiraled inward. That process produced X-ray radiation along with a powerful "wind" of gas. The outflow collided with material the star had released before its destruction, generating the bright blue optical and ultraviolet emission seen during the first few days, as well as the radio and millimeter signals detected by astronomers.

Researchers believe the shock "fizzles" after reaching the outer boundary of a bubble created by gas that the doomed star had previously expelled.

A Strange Signal Emerges From the Aftermath

One puzzling feature remains. Observations from Keck Observatory, Magellan Observatory, and the Very Large Telescope showed no recognizable chemical signatures during the first month after the explosion. As the event began to fade, however, weak signatures of hydrogen and helium gas appeared.

The helium produced an especially unexpected clue. It was traveling along the line of sight at more than 6,000 kilometers per second, indicating that a densely bound structure may have survived the initial blast and was now moving rapidly toward us.

The researchers speculate that the signal could come from a "stream" of material released by the star's core while the black hole's immense gravity was tearing it apart. A more speculative possibility is that the material comes from a third member of the system that is being blasted by the fast wind of particles and X-ray radiation generated by the feeding black hole.
articles.reasoning: The article reports a rare and significant astronomical observation of a black hole shredding a massive star, producing one of the most energetic stellar explosions ever recorded. This discovery advances understanding of black hole formation, growth, and extreme cosmic events, offering broad scientific impact and inspiring curiosity about the universe.
articles.personality_title: Astronomers witness rare black hole tearing apart a massive star
articles.personality_presentation:
**Context** – Scientists study black holes and stars to understand how the universe works. Sometimes, black holes pull in and destroy stars in events called Tidal Disruption Events, which release huge amounts of energy.

**What happened** – In early 2024, astronomers observed a giant star being shredded by a black hole in a dramatic event nicknamed “the Whippet.” This event released energy about 400 billion times stronger than our Sun’s output and sent a shock wave moving at one-fifth the speed of light. They used powerful telescopes on Earth and in space to watch the star’s destruction and the bright light and X-rays it produced.

**Impact** – This is one of the most powerful star-destroying events ever seen. It helps scientists learn how black holes grow by feeding on stars and shows a new way to find black holes in space. The discovery is special because the star’s remains may have survived in some form, moving quickly after the blast, which is something never seen before.

**What’s next step** – Researchers will keep studying the strange signals from the star’s remains to understand if part of the star or another object survived. They will also look for similar events to learn more about how black holes affect their surroundings and how often these rare cosmic explosions happen.

**One-sentence takeaway** – Astronomers have captured a rare and extremely powerful event where a black hole tore apart a massive star, revealing new clues about how black holes grow and survive such violent encounters.
articles.personality_title_fr: Les astronomes observent un trou noir déchirer une étoile massive
articles.personality_presentation_fr:
**Contexte** – Les scientifiques étudient les trous noirs et les étoiles pour comprendre le fonctionnement de l’univers. Parfois, les trous noirs attirent et détruisent des étoiles lors d’événements appelés événements de perturbation gravitationnelle, qui libèrent d’énormes quantités d’énergie.

**Ce qui s’est passé** – Début 2024, des astronomes ont observé une étoile géante déchirée par un trou noir dans un événement spectaculaire surnommé « le Whippet ». Cet événement a libéré une énergie environ 400 milliards de fois plus forte que celle de notre Soleil et a envoyé une onde de choc se déplaçant à un cinquième de la vitesse de la lumière. Ils ont utilisé de puissants télescopes terrestres et spatiaux pour suivre la destruction de l’étoile et la lumière brillante ainsi que les rayons X produits.

**Impact** – C’est l’un des événements de destruction d’étoile les plus puissants jamais observés. Cela aide les scientifiques à comprendre comment les trous noirs grandissent en se nourrissant des étoiles et montre une nouvelle façon de détecter les trous noirs dans l’espace. La découverte est spéciale car il semble qu’une partie des restes de l’étoile ait survécu et se déplace rapidement après l’explosion, ce qui est inédit.

**Prochaine étape** – Les chercheurs vont continuer à étudier les signaux étranges provenant des restes de l’étoile pour comprendre si une partie de l’étoile ou un autre objet a survécu. Ils chercheront aussi d’autres événements similaires pour en apprendre davantage sur l’effet des trous noirs sur leur environnement et la fréquence de ces explosions cosmiques rares.

**En une phrase** – Les astronomes ont capturé un événement rare et extrêmement puissant où un trou noir a déchiré une étoile massive, révélant de nouveaux indices sur la croissance des trous noirs et la survie à ces rencontres violentes.
articles.personality_title_es: Astrónomos observan un agujero negro desgarrando una estrella masiva
articles.personality_presentation_es:
**Contexto** – Los científicos estudian agujeros negros y estrellas para entender cómo funciona el universo. A veces, los agujeros negros atraen y destruyen estrellas en eventos llamados eventos de interrupción por marea, que liberan enormes cantidades de energía.

**Qué pasó** – A principios de 2024, los astrónomos vieron cómo un agujero negro desgarraba una estrella gigante en un evento espectacular llamado “el Whippet”. Este evento liberó una energía unas 400 mil millones de veces mayor que la de nuestro Sol y envió una onda de choque moviéndose a una quinta parte de la velocidad de la luz. Usaron telescopios potentes en la Tierra y en el espacio para observar la destrucción de la estrella y la luz brillante y rayos X que produjo.

**Impacto** – Este es uno de los eventos más poderosos de destrucción estelar jamás vistos. Ayuda a los científicos a entender cómo los agujeros negros crecen alimentándose de estrellas y muestra una nueva forma de encontrar agujeros negros en el espacio. El descubrimiento es especial porque parece que parte de los restos de la estrella sobrevivió y se mueve rápidamente después de la explosión, algo nunca antes visto.

**Próximo paso** – Los investigadores seguirán estudiando las señales extrañas de los restos de la estrella para entender si una parte de la estrella o algún otro objeto sobrevivió. También buscarán eventos similares para aprender más sobre cómo los agujeros negros afectan su entorno y con qué frecuencia ocurren estas explosiones cósmicas raras.

**Una frase clave** – Los astrónomos capturaron un evento raro y muy poderoso donde un agujero negro desgarró una estrella masiva, revelando nuevas pistas sobre cómo crecen los agujeros negros y sobreviven a encuentros violentos.
